title: Continuous local formal morphisms and formal pullback cones
statement: For a ringed space $X$ [def-per-adic-formal-geometry], a section topology assigns a topology to each $\mathcal O_X(U)$. Such topologies are adic formal if every point has an open formal affine chart $\operatorname{Spf}(R,K)\to X$, with $R$ Noetherian and $K$-adically complete, on which all section topologies are carried homeomorphically to the inverse-limit section topologies [def-per-adic-principal-chart-data]. A ringed-space morphism $f:X\to Y$ is a continuous formal morphism if its maps on all section rings are continuous and its maps on all stalks are local ring homomorphisms. A formal pullback cone consists of four such spaces and continuous formal maps $p:P\to X$, $q:P\to Y$, $f:X\to S$, $g:Y\to S$, with $fp=gq$, such that every compatible pair of continuous formal maps from any locally Noetherian adic formal test space $T$ factors through a unique continuous formal map $T\to P$. The test space need not be quasi-compact and the maps need not preserve a chosen ideal of definition.
